Number of People Sentenced to Prison up by 11% since 2022 Calls for service are up Jail Bookings are on the rise JAILS ARE OVER CAPACITY Front end: increasing public safety need IDOC: contributing factors driving all-time high prison population BACK end: Fewer seeking Parole Solutions: criminal justice populations on the rise: strategies for safe management Idaho's incarcerated population is at an all-time high, recently surpassing 10,000 people. System-wide trends indicate this growth is not slowing down. Resources to support Idaho's public safety entities, from patrol to county jails and corrections, have not kept pace with Idaho's population growth. There is an urgent need for statewide strategies that manage current demands and plan for long-term public safety. • Parole grant rates are stable • Since 2022, the number of people having parole hearings has dropped by 14.6% • Number of people choosing to complete their sentence has increased by 52% • Increases in felony drug sentences signal a need for expanded secure substance use treatment. • Factors such as longer sentences, more people being sentenced to prison, time between parole hearings, and fewer people being sentenced to retained jurisdiction, all contribute to unprecedented prison growth. Despite stable parole grant rates, a drop in parole hearings and more people choosing to complete their sentence in prison means fewer parole releases. Drug crimes account for 24% of statewide crimes but 50% of people in IDOC custody IDOC prison population at all-time high with more than 1,800 in jails or out of state The number of new admissions has increased and an increasing percentage are sentenced to term, while the percentage sentenced to retained jurisdiction is down. 1. Increase out of state prison beds in the short-term 2. Enhance information sharing between counties and State for long-term planning 3. Operationalize new IDOC-run infrastructure as efficiently as possible, including the expansion of Community Reentry Center beds 4. Explore public-private partnerships to expand bed capacity 5. Consider building treatment facilities to reduce substance use problems statewide at lower cost than prison December 2025 Law enforcement agencies in Canyon County have experienced a 36% increase in calls for service since 2022 Bonneville County Jail bookings have increased by 25% since 2022 Ada County Jail has operated above capacity 349 days of the last year As the total State population continues to grow, crime rates remain low but there's an increase in volume of criminal activity. This places greater demands on law enforcement systems, underscoring the need for increased resources and system-wide strategies to manage rising public safety demands. 72% of people come in or return to IDOC on new charges 28% of people enter IDOC with only a technical violation of supervision Overall, admissions to IDOC are up, releases are down and more people are staying their full term. on average, people stay incarcerated for seven years In 2025, the median fixed term of incarceration is 7 years
